question: Where does version 1.3 establish and consume a Great General attachment, and why can culture-border displacement separate the linked records?

scope.boundary: This packet closes the static attachment and culture-border displacement gate. It classifies bulk unload only at the command-consumer boundary and does not map transport ownership, establish a runtime probe, or specify a repair.

dependencies.use: accepted command 17 Move path, unit table, record stride, movement executor, and presentation ordering
accepted command 0 resolver boundary and post-combat movement exits

currentEvidence.method: foreground read-only Ghidra queries against the pinned version 1.3 project, with exact raw words and narrow generated-code corroboration
currentEvidence.qualification: The configured Ghidra database truncates several functions after Xenon save-register thunks. Raw words establish the bounded instructions; generated code is used only to recover the surrounding indexed-address arithmetic and control flow. No runtime observation was made for this packet.

type30Definition.result: The pinned image independently confirms that special type 30 has zero base attack and zero base defense. A detached live record is therefore a combatless special unit, not a Great Person record or command payload; unit-record +0x03 remains separate identity or subtype state.
type30Definition.qualification: Only the already-accepted +0x40 attack and +0x41 defense field meanings are used. Adjacent definition byte +0x42 remains unnamed in current-image evidence even though external documentation describes two movement points.

externalCorroboration.result: The page describes the Great General as a zero-attack, zero-defense special unit that remains attached, and records a naval-disembark split that leaves the General independently attackable.
externalCorroboration.qualification: The page labels the glitch as Nintendo DS-specific. That platform restriction is not accepted as a current-image fact, and the page does not establish the Xbox executable path or transaction ordering.

attachment.offsetCorrection: The movement and deletion scans keep their cursor at record +0x0C. Their lhz/sth operand 0x44 therefore addresses record +0x50, not record +0x44.
livePredicate: the candidate comes from the carrier's same-player 256-record table
record flags at +0x0C do not have the high dead bit set
the signed halfword at +0x50 equals the live carrier unit id

ordinaryMoveConsumer.completionResult: The conditional branch at 0x82CDF438 returns to the linked-record scan while the unit index is below 256. Address 0x82CDF43C is the first instruction after that scan completes and is a bounded ordinary-Move probe completion edge.
ordinaryMoveConsumer.result: After moving the addressed unit, command 17 scans live same-player records and moves every record whose signed +0x50 link names that unit. The scan is generic, so a Great General repair must retain the type-30 discriminator.

attachmentEstablishment.creator: 0x82D11750
attachmentEstablishment.result: The branch creates a type-30 record, recalculates its movement budget, and stores the addressed unit id from r15 into the created record's +0x50 halfword. Command 24's +0x03 store is separate identity state and is not the carrier link.
attachmentEstablishment.qualification: The vendored command labels are a lead only. The current-image type, creator call, and link store are authoritative; the higher-level distinction between command cases 25 and 44 remains unnamed here.

deletion.result: The second live-record scan compares effective record +0x50 with the deleted unit id. A matched type-30 record is recursively deleted, then the scan writes -1 through the same +0x50 field. This is a death cleanup edge, not evidence of a surviving intentional detach operation.

borderDisplacement.result: The producer chooses an adjacent valid destination, commits +0x1C/+0x1E directly, otherwise falls back to accepted city coordinates or deletes the record. The culture caller reaches it while sweeping eligible live records at affected tiles.
borderDisplacement.type30Treatment: The producer never reads type 30 or +0x50. The culture caller also does not use +0x50. Type 30's definition flag word is 0x00008000 at 0x82F71280, so it is not excluded by the caller's 0x00080000 definition-flag test and can be displaced independently of its carrier.

genericChildPropagation.result: The producer propagates coordinates only to live children whose signed +0x26 relation names the moved unit. It does not include Great General +0x50 attachments.

borderDisplacement.completionResult: 0x82CBF534 is reached after every displacement-producer call in the culture sweep and before its one conditional presentation call. The call at 0x82CBF548 returns to 0x82CBF54C, which is the first post-presentation-call completion edge and is followed by no further displacement. A bounded guarded operation has both a pre-presentation window at 0x82CBF534 and a completion edge at 0x82CBF54C; the completed form is duplicable after the existing overrun movement-executor returns at 0x82CDFA64 and 0x82CDFCC4.

bulkUnloadClassification.result: The current command consumer exposes no distinct unload-all case and the command 17 Move branch does not call 0x82CF2F60. It moves one addressed unit through 0x82CD69B8 and then performs the +0x50 linked scan. A bulk-unload symptom therefore belongs to producer-side sequencing of ordinary Move transactions or another transport transaction, not the culture-border producer.
bulkUnloadClassification.qualification: The UI-side unload-all loop and transport-link rewrite order were not recovered. They require a separate packet and are not evidence for changing generic cargo behavior in this topic.

acceptance.unambiguousLiveAttachmentPredicate: live same-player type 30 with signed +0x50 equal to the live carrier unit id
acceptance.safeDuplicableEdge: 0x82CBF54C after the presentation call; duplicate only after successful overrun executor returns
remainingUnknowns: runtime values and final ordering for one culture-growth incident
the UI-side bulk-unload transaction and any transport-link rewrites
a surviving intentional detach producer, if one exists outside the bounded deletion neighborhood
multiplayer checksum coverage for the derived border sweep
the exact build, record values, and hostile-attack sequence from the culture-growth incident

staticQuery.truncationGuard: Zero instruction or reference results in thunk-truncated functions were not treated as negative evidence.

guards: No runtime probe is established here; any probe remains default-off and read-only.
Do not treat cursor-relative operand 0x44 as unit-record offset 0x44; the effective carrier link is +0x50.
Do not reconcile generic +0x50-linked records without the live same-player type-30 discriminator.
Do not restore a deleted type-30 record or overwrite the -1 death-cleanup sentinel.
Do not confuse the live type-30 special unit with a Great Person identity, award, or command payload.
Do not infer the bulk-unload transaction, transport ownership, or transport-link rewrite order from command 17 consumption.
Do not alter presentation count, command completion, ownership, movement budget, identity, or generic +0x26 child behavior.
conclusion: Version 1.3 establishes a Great General attachment by storing the carrier unit id in type 30's +0x50 halfword. Ordinary Move follows that link, but culture-border displacement calls 0x82CF2F60 independently for eligible records and propagates only the separate +0x26 child relation. The sweep reaches a pre-presentation edge at 0x82CBF534 and the first post-call completion edge at 0x82CBF54C, giving the bounded operation a completion form duplicable after successful overrun movement. Bulk unload is separate at the command-consumer boundary.
